classification.difficultyReason: Requires combining ordinates of piecewise-linear and curved graphs, recognising cancellation and retaining the common domain.

content.prompt: Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$, graph $y=f(x)+g(x)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Printed page 40, question 16, upper-left cell of range 16–19
spec.description: Two upward V-shaped component graphs intersect at the origin. Their vertices are below the x-axis, symmetrically to the left and right of the y-axis. Both outer branches have arrowheads. Axes have x and y labels, without ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: Dimensionless drawing coordinates preserve the depicted equal branch slopes, opposite vertex positions and intersection. Coordinates are construction parameters, not additional numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Component graphs only; the sum is absent.

answer.short: A horizontal segment on the $x$-axis between the two component vertices, with straight branches rising outwards on both sides.
answer.worked: Between the two vertices, the ordinates are equal and opposite, so their sum is zero. Outside this interval, both ordinates increase as you move away from the centre. Add the ordinates on each vertical line to obtain the two rising straight branches.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 16; answer PDF page 6, printed page 310, label 16
spec.description: Complete sum graph with a central segment on the x-axis and two rising outer rays; component graphs are dashed.
spec.mathematics: Adding the component ordinates gives zero between the vertices and outer rays with twice the component branch slope.

spec.sourceRegion: Printed page 40, question 17, upper-right cell of range 16–19
spec.description: Two upward V-shaped graphs have vertices on opposite sides of the x-axis origin and intersect on the positive y-axis. Outer branches have arrowheads; no ticks or grid are printed.
spec.mathematics: Dimensionless construction coordinates preserve symmetric vertex positions on the x-axis, equal branch slopes and the common positive y-intercept. No numerical values are displayed.

answer.short: A horizontal segment above the $x$-axis between the two vertices, at twice the common $y$-intercept, with straight branches rising outwards.
answer.worked: Between the vertices, one ordinate increases by the same amount that the other decreases, so the sum is constant. At the $y$-axis, the two equal ordinates add to twice their common height. Outside the vertices, adding the ordinates gives two rising straight branches.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 17; answer PDF page 6, printed page 310, label 17
spec.description: Complete sum graph with a positive horizontal central segment and rising outer rays; dashed components remain visible.
spec.mathematics: The central sum is twice the common component y-intercept. Each outer ray has twice the component branch slope. The complete solution uses an extended vertical frame to show the increased height.

spec.sourceRegion: Printed page 40, question 18, lower-left cell of range 16–19
spec.description: An upward V has its vertex at the origin and arrowheads on both outer branches. An upper semicircle centred at the origin has endpoints on the x-axis. Axes have no numerical ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: A unit semicircle and slope-one V are dimensionless construction geometry matching the source proportions; no radius, coordinates or equations are supplied to students.

answer.short: A symmetric curve with two humps and a central corner. The centre is at the semicircle's highest point; the two endpoints are at the corresponding heights of the V. Use only the semicircle's domain.
answer.worked: At each semicircle endpoint, its ordinate is zero, so the sum has the same ordinate as the V. At the $y$-axis, the V has ordinate zero, so the sum has the semicircle's height. Between these positions, add the positive semicircle ordinate to the V ordinate. This gives a hump on each side of the central corner. The sum is defined only where both component graphs exist.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 18; answer PDF page 6, printed page 310, label 18
spec.description: A complete symmetric two-humped sum curve with a central corner and two filled endpoints, over dashed component graphs.
spec.mathematics: The ordinate sum is constructed on the closed semicircle domain only. The parametric construction adds the V ordinate to the semicircle ordinate without introducing printed numerical givens.

spec.sourceRegion: Printed page 40, question 19, lower-right cell of range 16–19
spec.description: An inverted V shares the top of an upper semicircle and passes through its two x-axis endpoints, then continues downwards outwards with arrowheads. Axes have no numerical ticks or grid.
spec.mathematics: Dimensionless construction geometry preserves the shared positive y-intercept and both common x-intercepts. No radius, scale or function formula is printed.

answer.short: A symmetric arch with a pointed central maximum at twice the common $y$-intercept and endpoints at the two common $x$-intercepts. Use only the semicircle's domain.
answer.worked: At each common $x$-intercept, both ordinates are zero, so the sum is zero. At the common $y$-intercept, the equal ordinates add to twice that height. Between these anchors, add the two positive ordinates to obtain the curved sides meeting at a pointed central maximum. The sum ends at the semicircle's endpoints.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 19; answer PDF page 6, printed page 310, label 19
spec.description: Complete symmetric sum arch with a pointed maximum and filled endpoints on the x-axis; component graphs are dashed.
spec.mathematics: The sum doubles the shared central height and retains the two common zero ordinates. The finite common domain excludes the inverted V's outer rays.
